title: Breaking a Quantity Apart
objective: A quantity can be broken apart in more than one way, and each way still gives back the same whole.
studentQuestion: Can you break this apart a different way?
newIdea: More than one decomposition exists for the same whole.

teaching.setup: 6 counters, already split one way (4 and 2) from a prior demonstration.
teaching.see: Is 4 and 2 the only way to break 6 apart?
teaching.break: Re-split the same 6 a different way (e.g. 3 and 3, or 5 and 1).
teaching.build: Record each split found, side by side.
teaching.transform: Several different-looking splits, all of the same whole (6) — the earliest concrete instance of many forms, one value.

check.prompt: Recombine each split and recount to confirm it's still 6 every time.

examples.second: 8 into at least two different splits.
examples.transfer: A number the learner has not yet split (e.g. 9), find as many splits as they can.

mastery.evidence: Produces at least two different splits of the same whole and confirms both recombine to the same total.
